# Purpose

`scripts/analyze_scores.R` summarizes a synthetic dataset of 300 students. It reports the number of students and the mean and median final score for each course, then draws two plots: the distribution of final scores, and study hours against final score with a regression line.

# Inputs

The script reads one file, `data/student_scores.csv`, created by `scripts/generate_data.R`.

| Column        | Description                                         |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `student_id`  | Unique student identifier                           |
| `course`      | Statistics, Databases, Programming or Data Visualization |
| `study_hours` | Weekly study hours                                  |
| `attendance`  | Attendance percentage                               |
| `final_score` | Final score out of 100                              |

# Outputs

| File                           | Description                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `outputs/course_summary.csv`   | Students, mean score and median score per course  |
| `outputs/score_distribution.png` | Histogram of final scores                       |
| `outputs/hours_vs_score.png`   | Scatter plot of study hours against final score   |

# Dependencies

```{r packages}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Walkthrough

## Load the data

```{r load-data}
scores <- read_csv("data/student_scores.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
glimpse(scores)
```

## Summarize scores by course

```{r course-summary}
course_summary <- scores |>
  group_by(course) |>
  summarise(
    students = n(),
    mean_score = round(mean(final_score), 1),
    median_score = round(median(final_score), 1),
    mean_study_hours = round(mean(study_hours), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_score))

knitr::kable(course_summary)
```

## Distribution of final scores

```{r score-distribution}
ggplot(scores, aes(x = final_score)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Final Scores", x = "Final score", y = "Number of students") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Study hours and final score

```{r hours-vs-score}
ggplot(scores, aes(x = study_hours, y = final_score)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "Study Hours vs Final Score", x = "Weekly study hours", y = "Final score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r correlation}
round(cor(scores$study_hours, scores$final_score), 2)
```

# How to Run

The script itself saves the plots and the summary table. Run it from the project root:

```{r run-script, eval=FALSE}
source("scripts/analyze_scores.R")
```
